title: ArborKV: Structure-Aware KV Cache Management for Scaling Tree-based LLM Reasoning
claim: Moving from linear to tree-structured search blows up memory, and sequence-centric eviction that flattens the tree discards branches still needed for backtracking.
layout: 2 stacked panels: (a) side-by-side linear vs tree, (b) top-down flow; red failure highlights
description: The figure has two labeled parts. Part (a) places two rounded boxes side by side. The left box, Chain-of-Thought, shows a chain v1 to v4 above stacked blue KV Cache blocks that grow in a staircase ("Linear Growth") and stay near a dashed red "Device Memory Budget" line. The right box, Tree-of-Thoughts, shows a branching tree with a solid active path and dashed faded inactive nodes. Next to it is a tall KV Cache stack labeled "Memory Explosion" that crosses the budget line, with a red X. Part (b) is a vertical three-band flow. First comes "Search Dynamics", a tree with a backtracking arrow. A "Naive Flattening" arrow leads to the "Flat-Sequence Assumption", a row of tokens with active ones bold and old ones greyed out. Last is a pink "Blind Spot" band where the evicted tokens are crossed out. A red arrow and the text "Expensive Recomputation / Reasoning Failure" mark the result. Blue marks active or retained items, grey marks inactive ones, and red marks failure.
caption: Challenges in Tree-structured Reasoning. (a) Transitioning from linear CoT to tree-based search leads to a KV-cache memory explosion that exhausts hardware budgets. (b) Sequence-centric policies flatten the tree into a linear pool, mistakenly evicting inactive branches required for future backtracking.
abstract: Recent progress in LLM reasoning has increasingly shifted from single-pass generation to explicit search over intermediate reasoning states. Tree-of-Thoughts (ToT) organizes inference to tree-structured search with branching and backtracking, but it substantially amplifies the Key--Value (KV) cache: retaining KV states for a frontier of partial trajectories quickly becomes a memory bottleneck that limits throughput and constrains search depth and width under fixed hardware budgets. We address this challenge by observing that KV reuse in ToT-style inference is governed by search dynamics: near-term decoding depends primarily on the active branch and its ancestors, whereas inactive subtrees have low short-term reuse probability yet must remain recoverable for backtracking. Motivated by this, we propose ArborKV, a structure-aware eviction framework that couples a lightweight value estimator with a tree-aware allocation policy, and performs purely token-extractive eviction with lazy rehydration to support revisits. Experiments on ToT-style reasoning benchmarks show that ArborKV achieves up to ~4x peak KV-memory reduction while preserving near-full-retention accuracy, enabling larger search configurations under fixed device budgets that would otherwise run out of memory.
